key_terms.meaning: Three ways to declare a variable; var is function-scoped and old, let and const are block-scoped, and const cannot be reassigned.
A statement such as if, else, switch, for, while or do-while that decides which other statements run and how many times.
A named block of statements that takes inputs (parameters), does work, and returns one value with return.
An ordered list of values reached by a numeric index starting at 0, written as [10, 20, 30] and measured by .length.
A collection of key-value pairs where each value is reached by its name, written as {name: "Ravi", marks: 82}.
A signal from the browser that something happened, such as a click, a key press or the page finishing load.
The default travel of an event upward from the target element through its parent, grandparent and so on to the document.
The first phase of event travel, going downward from the document to the target when the listener is registered with capture set to true.
Document Object Model: the tree of nodes the browser builds from your HTML, which JavaScript can read and change.
A node that represents one HTML tag in the DOM tree, such as a div or a p, and can have attributes and children.
Browser Object Model: the objects outside the page, mainly window, navigator, location, history and screen.
ES6 shorthand (a, b) => a + b that is shorter than function syntax and takes this from the surrounding code.
A file that shares code with export and loads it elsewhere with import, keeping each file's names private by default.
A function passed into another function to be called later, once the slow work finishes or the event fires.
An object with three states — pending, fulfilled, rejected — that settles once and delivers a value or an error to .then and .catch.
Syntax that makes a function return a promise and lets you write await in front of it so asynchronous code reads like straight-line code.
The browser object that sends an HTTP request in the background and reports progress through readyState and onreadystatechange.
JavaScript Object Notation: a text format of objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false and null used to send data between client and server.
Document Type Definition: an older grammar for an XML document listing its allowed elements, attributes and nesting order.
An XML-written contract (XSD) that defines allowed elements, attributes and data types, and is itself valid XML.
A small JavaScript library that wraps selection, events and AJAX in short chained calls behind one global name, $ or jQuery.

takeaways: A JavaScript program is a list of statements; variables store values, operators combine them, and control statements choose the path.
Functions, arrays and objects are the three containers that let you stop repeating code and start organising data.
An event fires on a target, travels down in capture and up in bubble, and your handler receives an event object describing it.
The browser turns HTML into a DOM tree of element, text and attribute nodes, and editing that tree is what makes a page dynamic.
ES6 gives block scope with let and const, short arrow functions, class syntax and modules, so big programs stay readable.
JavaScript has one call stack, so slow work goes to the browser and returns through the event loop into callbacks, promises or await.
AJAX sends a request with XMLHttpRequest or fetch, gets back text or JSON, and patches the page without a reload.
XML describes data as nested tags; a DTD or an XML Schema is the contract that says which tags may appear and in what order.
jQuery shortens selection, events and AJAX into chained calls that behave alike across browsers.
bank_note: Long answers in this unit usually ask you to explain a mechanism (event flow, the DOM tree, the event loop, AJAX states) and then show working code, so keep a short correct snippet ready for each.

bank.q: Explain variables, operators and control statements in JavaScript. Give one small example for each kind of control statement.
outline: var is function-scoped and hoisted; let and const are block-scoped; const blocks reassignment but not mutation of an object
Operators: arithmetic, comparison with == versus ===, logical && || !, assignment and ternary
if / else if / else, switch with break, for, while, do-while, for-of and for-in
One example each: a grade decided by if-else, a menu by switch, a sum by for loop

bank.q: Explain functions, arrays and objects in JavaScript, including parameters, return values and the difference between an array and an object.
outline: Function declaration is hoisted; function expression and arrow function are not usable before their line
Parameters versus arguments; return ends the function and hands back one value
Array: ordered, zero-based index, length, push, pop, slice, and iteration with for or forEach
Object: named keys, dot and bracket access, nested objects, delete; array when order matters, object when names matter

bank.q: Explain the three phases of event flow in the DOM and how addEventListener registers a handler in each phase.
outline: Capture phase runs from window down to the parent of the target
Target phase runs on the element where the event occurred
Bubble phase runs upward from the target to the document
addEventListener(type, handler, useCapture) — false or omitted means bubble, true means capture
stopPropagation stops further travel; preventDefault cancels the browser's own action

bank.q: What is AJAX? Explain the XMLHttpRequest object, its readyState values and the call-back methods used.
outline: AJAX: background HTTP request plus partial page update, no full reload
open(method, url, async), setRequestHeader, send
readyState 0 unsent, 1 opened, 2 headers received, 3 loading, 4 done
onreadystatechange checks readyState 4 and status 200
responseText versus responseXML; the same origin rule and CORS

bank.q: Explain DTD and XML Schema. How does an XML Schema improve on a DTD?
outline: XML: prolog, one root element, nested elements, attributes, well-formed versus valid
DTD: ELEMENT, ATTLIST, ENTITY declarations; sequence, choice, occurrence symbols * + ?
XML Schema: written in XML, supports data types such as xs:integer, xs:date, xs:minOccurs and maxOccurs
DTD has no data types and its own syntax; Schema is namespaced, typed and reusable
Both answer: which tags, which attributes, in what order, how many times

bank.q: Write a JavaScript program that reads marks of five students into an array, passes the array to a function, and prints the average and the highest mark using a loop.
outline: Array literal of five numbers; .length used in the loop condition
Function takes the array as a parameter and returns two values, for example an object {average, highest}
Loop accumulates a sum; a comparison variable tracks the maximum
Average = sum / length; guard against an empty array
Output written with console.log or into a page element

bank.q: Write HTML and JavaScript that build a list from an array using createElement, textContent and appendChild, and delete one item when it is clicked.
outline: Get the container with document.getElementById or querySelector
Loop the array, createElement('li'), set textContent, appendChild to the list
Append the list to the document once, not on every pass, for speed
Click handler on the list using bubbling, then event.target to find the item
removeChild or element.remove() to delete; explain why the handler is attached to the parent

bank.q: Write a form with name and email fields and validate it in JavaScript using addEventListener, showing error messages beside the fields.
outline: Attach a submit listener and call preventDefault to stop the page reload
Read values with element.value; trim spaces before checking
Check for empty name; check email against a simple pattern with a regular expression
Show or clear the error text by setting textContent on a span
Return false or use preventDefault so bad data never leaves the page

bank.q: Write code that fetches JSON data from a server with XMLHttpRequest, and rewrite the same code using fetch with async/await.
outline: xhr.open('GET', url, true); onreadystatechange checks readyState 4 and status 200
JSON.parse(xhr.responseText) turns the reply into an object
fetch(url) returns a promise; await response.json() returns the parsed body
try / catch around await to handle network and HTTP errors
Both versions then patch the DOM with the received values

bank.q: Convert a given ES5 block of code to ES6 using let and const, an arrow function, a class and a module export.
outline: Replace var with const by default and let only where reassignment happens
Arrow function for the callback, noting this is taken from the enclosing scope
class with constructor and method, extending with super where needed
export the class and import it in another file; mention type="module"
Name the behaviour changes, not only the shorter syntax

bank.q: Using jQuery, select a set of list items, hide them, and load data from the server on a button click, explaining each chained call.
outline: $('li') returns a jQuery collection; each method returns the same collection so calls chain
hide() and show() change the display style; text() or html() set content
$.ajax or $.get with url, dataType 'json' and a done call-back
Append results with append() after clearing the list
Compare with the plain DOM version to show the shorter code

bank.q: Compare callbacks, promises and async/await for asynchronous JavaScript. Explain the event loop and how each style handles an error.
outline: Single call stack, web APIs hand off slow work, the event loop moves ready call-backs into the stack
Callback: nesting causes callback hell, error passed as the first argument
Promise: three states, settles once, .then chaining, .catch for errors, Promise.all for parallel work
async/await: reads top to bottom, errors caught with try/catch
Microtasks from promises run before the next timer task; state the order for a mixed example

bank.q: Compare XML and JSON as data formats for a web application. Give the case where each is the better choice.
outline: XML: tags, attributes, supports schemas, DTD, namespaces, XSLT; verbose
JSON: built from JS object syntax, short, parsed directly by JSON.parse, no schema in the core
XML suits documents, mixed content, strict validation and existing enterprise or SOAP services
JSON suits browser-server API payloads and mobile clients where size matters
Evaluate on size, parsing speed, readability and validation, not only on preference

bank.q: Explain event delegation. Using bubbling, show how one listener on a list can handle clicks on all its items, and evaluate its cost and limits.
outline: A click on an item bubbles to the list; the listener on the list catches it
event.target is the clicked element, event.currentTarget is the listener's element
closest() or a tag check identifies which item was clicked
Saves memory and works for items added later
Limits: events that do not bubble, deep trees and the need to filter unrelated targets

bank.q: Describe the full path of a button click that loads data and updates the page: DOM event, AJAX request, server, JSON reply, DOM patch. Say what fails at each stage and how you would find it.
outline: Event listener fires, handler reads form values and builds the request
fetch or XMLHttpRequest sends an HTTP GET or POST; network panel shows status, headers and body
Server route handles the request and returns JSON with a status code
Response parsed, errors caught; loading and error states shown to the user
DOM updated with textContent or created elements; console and breakpoints used to trace each step

glossary.def: A single instruction in a JavaScript program, normally ended by a semicolon.
A named box in memory that holds a value until you assign a new one.
The way declarations are moved to the top of their scope before the code runs, so var exists but is undefined early.
The part of the program where a given name can be seen.
A symbol such as +, ===, && or ?: that combines values into a new value.
Any value that behaves as true in a condition; only false, 0, "", null, undefined and NaN are falsy.
A name listed in a function definition that receives an argument when the function is called.
The actual value passed into a function call.
The position of an item in an array, counted from 0.
A named value stored on an object, read with dot or bracket notation.
A function stored as a property of an object and called through that object.
The function registered to run when a particular event fires.
The registration made by addEventListener that ties an event type to a handler.
The element on which the event actually happened, found at event.target.
The object the browser passes to a handler, carrying type, target, key, coordinates and methods such as preventDefault.
One item in the DOM tree: an element, a text run, an attribute or the document itself.
Changing the DOM, styles and content from JavaScript after the page has loaded.
The list of functions currently running, with the newest call on top.
The browser mechanism that moves ready call-backs from the queues onto the call stack when it is empty.
Wrapping an old callback-based function so that it returns a promise instead.
Turning an object into text for sending, as JSON.stringify does.
XML that obeys the syntax rules: one root, closed tags, quoted attributes.
XML that is well-formed and also obeys its DTD or XML Schema.
A pattern such as #id or .card that names which elements you want, used by jQuery and querySelector.
